water.title: Water: rain, tanks and valves
water.none: No water mapped for this guild yet. A WormBed5 catches rain from the roof in a barrel whose tap refills the tank pipes, and its worm box's liquid goes by a valve to the tank pipes or to a tank in the garden.
water.budget: From April to September rain covers about {share} % of what the bed uses (litres a month, from the area's climate):
water.warn.lost: In {n} months the barrel overflows: a larger barrel, or a second one, would keep more of the rain.
water.warn.dry: In {n} summer months the catchment hardly refills the tank pipes: a larger roof surface would help.
water.note: Rules of thumb (use: Hargreaves from the month's warmth and sun); the Learn view's H7 checks them against the real bed. Worm liquid never goes into a store kept for clean water. Monthly averages hide dry spells: a summer has weeks without rain, and only the barrel's size bridges them.
learn.intro: What this habitat is learning. Each guild runs cycles of plan, do, check and act: hypotheses with the range in which they hold, the measures that test them, the measured values, and what was changed. The guild's edge sees them too.
learn.noGuild: No Perma5Guild yet: make one on the Overview, then come back to plan what it should learn.
learn.about.PlanPhase: Plan: say what you expect and how sure you are; set the numbers to your own bed before measuring starts.
learn.about.DoPhase: Do: run the guild and add the measured values as they come. Each dot is a value; the green band is the range in which the hypothesis holds.
learn.about.CheckPhase: Check: the season's values beside the hypotheses. A hypothesis fails when two values running lie outside its range, or the last one does.
learn.about.ActPhase: Act: write what you change for each hypothesis that failed, set its numbers to what you learned, and start the next cycle.
learn.why: Why, and how it is measured
learn.actPlaceholder: e.g. less liquid than thought: the twin's model set to 0.10 l/kg; sump kept

wb.what.single.hint: One bed with its worm box at one end, worked by a Gantry5-gen1 robot: a roof, a terrace, a corner of the garden.

sets.title: Plant sets
sets.how: How a set becomes a bed
sets.how.1: Each chosen set gets its share of the free room, and each of its plants its share within the set.
sets.how.2: The room is turned into plant numbers by each plant's spacing.
sets.how.3: The biggest plants go in first, tall ones along the side where they shade nothing; the little ones last.
sets.how.4: Low ground covers go last, under tall plants where that suits them.
sets.how.5: Then plants are swapped and moved while it improves: good neighbours together, bad neighbours and relatives apart, the soil covered.
sets.how.layers: Layers: a plant 70 cm or taller is tall; a low plant that covers the soil (40 cm or less) is a ground cover and may share a tall plant's room. No other plants share room.
sets.how.caveat: Neighbours follow traditional companion-planting guidance, not trials. The bed shows what holds: keep what works, change what does not.
sets.relatives: Relatives (they share pests, so they are spread out):
sets.layout.bed: An example: this set alone in a bed of {l} × {w} cm, {d} cm deep, with a {box} cm worm box at the right end. Your bed's plan differs with its size and what already grows in it.
